claim: The wpnews.pro reprint of the CMP 170HX dual-card writeup reproduces the original gist's benchmark table exactly, so the aggregator did not distort the numbers.
stance_target: The reliability of the wpnews.pro note as evidence for the P2P and prefill claims
scope_conditions: Direct comparison of the gist (ropuls/d2978531ba3a1a183e70f62f3de2eb84) against the wpnews.pro article, both fetched 2026-10-27

claim: The P2P recipe is amoghmunikote/cmpunlocker as the base plus three bayley/cmpunlocker patches pinned to exact commits, and the regkey alone was never verified sufficient.
stance_target: How reproducible the P2P enablement is, which bounds how heavily the training-feasibility analysis should lean on it
scope_conditions: cmpunlocker master 6c442ee, bayley patches at 5a7bb4b, ROMED8-2T host
quoted_support: Not tested: whether the regkey alone, without the three patches, is enough. An earlier version of this gist said so; that was not verified.

claim: The first P2P setup was not reproducible for some users, and the revised recipe pins exact commits and adds UEFI and kernel prerequisites.
stance_target: Whether the P2P result generalises to the repo's box, which the repo's documentation does not address
scope_conditions: ROMED8-2T UEFI-only board, Proxmox VE kernel 7.0.14-pve
quoted_support: Update 2026-10-02. The initial setup here was not reproducible for some people (P2P did not come up). This is the revised setting: amogh's cmpunlocker as the base, patched selectively with three P2P patches from bayley/cmpunlocker, pinned to exact commits

claim: Re-enabling reserved TPCs via cmpunlocker master raises the SM count from 70 to 74 per card, which yields only about +1.8% prefill at a fixed power cap.
stance_target: Whether SM count is a meaningful throughput lever on this card, which affects achievable TFLOPS estimates
scope_conditions: cmpunlocker master 6c442ee versus v0.4, both cards at the power cap
quoted_support: Prefill is compute-bound, but both cards sit at the power cap, so +4 SM gave only about +1.8%. With the +200 offset the SMs pay off: about +7% decode and +6% prefill at the same 200 W
